chunks: And my father narrated to me (may Allah have mercy on him) from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-‘Amrakī ibn ‘Alī al-Būfakī, from Yaḥyā – who was in the service of Abī Ja‘far the Second – from ‘Īsā ibn Sulaymān, from Muḥammad ibn Mārid, from his aunt, who said: I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) say:
Verily, in the clay of the Ḥā’ir, where al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) is buried, is a cure for every disease and protection from every fear.

key_terms.الْحَائِر: Al-Hā’ir, a specific location in Karbala where Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) is buried.
key_terms.طِين: Clay or earth, specifically referring to the soil of the grave.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of the clay from the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh transmits this report through a chain reaching Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.), establishing the clay of al-Ha'ir as a tangible medium of barakah (blessing) and shifa (healing). This tradition underscores the Shia belief in the intercessory power of the Ahl al-Bayt, where physical elements associated with them serve as conduits for divine protection and cure, reflecting the cosmic significance of Karbala.
